01 / Problem & goal

Make public railway data easy to explore, not just download.

Historical ridership data is useful, but its value is harder to see when it is scattered across files, time periods and different levels of detail.

THE PROBLEM

Fragmented information

Station locations and passenger counts come from different official datasets. Some statistics are station-level; others are line- or operator-level.

OUR SOLUTION

A connected web explorer

Link the rail map, station details and historical timeline. Let visitors navigate through space and time with clear, responsive controls.

OUR PRINCIPLE

No invented detail

Show a metric only at its available granularity. A monthly total stays monthly; organization-level figures are not presented as station counts.

Proposed research question

How can historical ridership information for Bangkok’s urban railway network be integrated and explored interactively across stations and time while preserving differences in data coverage?

03 / Approved data sources

Built around Thailand Open Government Data.

All planned primary data sources are on data.go.th, one of the approved sources for this course. The exact usable records and line-level coverage still need file-level verification.

01 — Network geography

Station and line master

Department of Rail Transport station codes, Thai/English names, coordinates and operational status. Intended as the geographic reference table.

View official dataset ↗
02 — Station statistics

Passenger arrivals / departures

Station-level passenger counts and dates. We will inspect the actual CSV for line coverage before enabling daily station histories across the network.

View official dataset ↗
03 — Network statistics

Rail system ridership

Historical daily, monthly and yearly operator/system passenger totals. These support broader trends, but must not be mislabeled as individual station counts.

View official dataset ↗
Already integrated for this prototype: Siam BTS station — 12 actual monthly passenger-journey totals from 2023. Bangkok Statistics 2023, Table 2-7 ↗ Source agency: Bangkok Metropolitan Administration; monthly records only.
Data quality rule: We will document which lines, stations, dates and granularities exist before publishing metrics. Missing detail will be marked “not available,” not filled with invented values.
04 / Method & research plan

From raw public data to interactive insight.

Our core method uses data cleaning, integration, OLAP-style aggregation and visual exploration, following CRISP-DM.

01

Understand

Define user questions about where and when passengers travel.

02

Collect

Retrieve official files and audit station, line and date coverage.

03

Prepare

Clean names, keys, date formats, gaps and aggregation levels.

04

Explore

Implement station drill-down, time roll-up and filter comparisons.

05

Evaluate

Validate totals, missing-data behavior and the user experience.

Data mining extension

Proposed secondary track: station-pattern clustering, pending data suitability and Ajarn’s approval.

With enough comparable station histories, we can group stations by demand patterns and compare clustering approaches such as K-means, hierarchical clustering and DBSCAN. We would evaluate clusters with appropriate unlabeled-data metrics such as silhouette score, not classification accuracy. This extension will not replace the interactive historical website.

05 / Planned outcomes

What our group will deliver.

We are proposing a research-informed web application, not claiming that the live data integration is already complete.

Interactive web application

A Bangkok rail map with two-click station focus, smooth zoom, search, a historical time explorer, available-granularity controls and line/station comparisons.

Documented government-data pipeline

Source inventory, schema mapping, cleaning steps, time aggregation and transparent coverage rules, with code and dataset documentation.

Evaluation & findings

Data-quality validation, exploratory comparisons and clear interpretations of historical patterns. Clustering evaluation if the extension is approved and feasible.

Final academic submission

CRISP-DM-based research paper, code, dataset references and a concise presentation demonstrating the website and explaining its findings.

RANGSIT UNIVERSITY INTERNATIONAL COLLEGE · ICT324 · MILESTONE 2 PROJECT PROPOSAL

Bangkok Rail Explorer: Interactive Historical Analytics Across Urban Railway Lines

Team: Kyaw Zaw Lin ([student ID omitted from public version]) · Aung Khant Tun ([student ID omitted from public version]) · Aung Kaung Sett Naing ([student ID omitted from public version])

Problem statement

Historical Bangkok rail passenger information is distributed across public datasets with different geographic and time coverage. Traditional tables and separate charts are difficult to explore across lines, stations, days, weeks and months. Our project proposes an interactive web application that connects a railway network map to historical ridership visualizations while clearly showing which levels of detail are supported by the source records.

Research question

How can historical ridership information for Bangkok’s urban railway network be integrated and explored interactively across stations and time while preserving differences in data coverage?

Dataset

Primary sources: Thailand Open Government Data (data.go.th), Department of Rail Transport (DRT).

  • Rail station/line master: line code, station code, names, latitude/longitude, operating status.
  • Station-level rail passengers: date, station, arrival and departure counts; actual line coverage to be audited.
  • Rail system passengers: daily/monthly/yearly system or operator totals, where station detail is unavailable.

Only real government data will be used for reported findings. We will verify record count, date range, gaps and granularity.

Planned technique

Data warehousing, preprocessing and OLAP-style historical exploration using time hierarchies and station/line dimensions. Our CRISP-DM workflow: understand, audit, clean, integrate, analyze, evaluate and deploy. A station clustering extension (K-means, hierarchical, DBSCAN) is under consideration, subject to instructor approval and comparable station histories.

Expected contribution

A map-first interactive historical dashboard supporting station selection, smooth zooming, time drill-down, trends and comparisons; a documented method for integrating government data without hiding missing detail; and interpretable historical insights for the public and transport researchers.

Official datasets: data.go.th/th/dataset/rail_station · data.go.th/th/dataset/drt2566_02 · data.go.th/th/dataset/stat_pass_rail
Project status: Concept and interaction prototype prepared; data audit and full integration remain planned work.
